first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent me this on the iPad because we're helping with the honeymoon as well as the wedding. I read it top to bottom. The opening is sensible: 'A number on its own tells you very little.' Fine, I'd rather be told to get it in writing than be shown a figure that changes later. It's calm, no slang, short paragraphs, and it talks about deposits, cancellation terms, insurance and insolvency, which are exactly the things I worry about. It treats practical questions as normal, which I appreciate. What it doesn't do is tell me who answers the phone if something goes wrong while they're away, or whether this company itself is covered if it goes under. Those I'd write down for Geoff and ask on a phone call.

journey.quote: A number on its own tells you very little. The useful questions are what the fee covers, how it is worked out and whether it is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Good. 'Agreed in writing before any work begins' is what I want to hear when it's our money. No figure, but I understand why.

journey.section: What you are paying a planner for
journey.quote: On a honeymoon with several stops, each booking brings its own deposit, its own deadline and its own fine print.
journey.reaction: Yes, that's precisely what frightens me about these trips. Someone has finally written it down plainly.

journey.section: What you are paying a planner for
journey.quote: What the fee does not buy is a different set of consumer rights.
journey.reaction: Honest. They're not pretending to be the government. I'd rather know where we stand.

journey.section: How planners may charge, as questions to ask
journey.quote: Do you receive commissions from the suppliers you book, and will you tell us which?
journey.reaction: That's the question Geoff would ask first. Pleased to see it on the list rather than tucked away.

journey.section: What the fee should cover, in writing
journey.quote: who to contact while you are travelling.
journey.reaction: Right, and that's my main worry. Who do they ring at 2am in another country? Glad it's on the list. I'll look for the answer further down.

journey.section: Paying in Australian dollars or another currency
journey.quote: Money transfer services in Australia must be registered with AUSTRAC, so check that before you use one.
journey.reaction: Practical. I'd not have known to check that, and it links to Moneysmart, which I trust.

journey.quote: Travel provider or agent insolvency is commonly left out of cancellation cover, and only some agents hold insolvency insurance, so ask your planner directly.
journey.reaction: This is my deposit question exactly. It's good advice, but now I want to know: does Wedded Wonderland hold it? The page tells me to ask and then doesn't say.

journey.section: How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: Honeymoon planning with us follows the same Wedded Advisor process as Wedded Concierge, whether the honeymoon follows a destination wedding or stands on its own.
journey.reaction: I had to read this twice. Is Wedded Concierge the service and Wedded Advisor the person? Plainer words would help someone my age.

journey.section: How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor looks after you from start to finish, as your single point of contact.
journey.reaction: A named person who stays with us. That's what I want. I'd still like to speak to them before anything is booked.

journey.section: How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and quotes in Australian dollars.
journey.reaction: AUD is reassuring. But 'your time zone' is Melbourne. When the children are in Europe and it's the middle of the night here, who picks up? The page asked that question earlier and doesn't answer it for itself.

journey.section: How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: So the questions above already have answers before you pay: what the fee is, what it covers and what each booking includes, all on paper.
journey.reaction: Some of them, yes. Not commissions, not insolvency cover, not who to call while travelling. It reads as a bit more than they've actually shown me.

journey.quote: Tell your Wedded Advisor the shape of the trip, agree the fee in writing before any work begins, and see every inclusion on paper before you commit.
journey.reaction: Sensible close. Everything in writing before money changes hands. I'd want it to say a phone call is how it starts.

unanswered_questions: Who do the couple ring if something goes wrong while they are overseas, outside Melbourne business hours? Is there after-hours support?
Does Wedded Wonderland hold insolvency insurance, and are our deposits protected if a supplier or Wedded Wonderland itself fails?
Is the first conversation a phone call, and can I (as a parent paying part) be on it?
What is the Difference between Wedded Concierge and a Wedded Advisor?
How is the Wedded Wonderland fee charged: flat, percentage or a mix, and roughly what range? (deferred business detail)
Does Wedded Wonderland receive commissions from the suppliers it books, and will it disclose them? (deferred business detail)
Is there a real honeymoon you've planned, with what it cost, so I can see an example? (deferred business detail)
Are there any perks or extras for couples who book with you? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: So the questions above already have answers before you pay: what the fee is, what it covers and what each booking includes, all on paper.
turn_offs_found.why: The page told me to ask about commissions, insolvency cover and who to contact while travelling, then says the questions 'already have answers' when those three aren't answered for Wedded Wonderland. It slightly oversells, and when it's my money I notice that.

would_share_with: My husband, the 'What the fee should cover, in writing' and 'Protecting what you pay' sections, with my questions about insolvency cover and after-hours contact written underneath
My daughter, the 'How planners may charge, as questions to ask' list, so she asks them before agreeing anything

cta_reaction.why: The page is sensible and the fee-in-writing promise is what I want. But I wouldn't fill in a form off this alone. I'd talk to Geoff first, and I'd want to know it leads to a phone call with a real person who can tell me who looks after the children at 2am overseas and whether our deposits are protected.

top_3_changes: In 'How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland', answer the article's own checklist item 'who to contact while you are travelling' for Wedded Wonderland (after-hours or in-trip support), only if the source pack supports it; otherwise soften 'So the questions above already have answers before you pay' so it doesn't claim more than the bullets show.

Clarify in one plain sentence how Wedded Concierge and Wedded Advisor relate (the service versus the person), since 'follows the same Wedded Advisor process as Wedded Concierge' reads as jargon to an older reader.
If sourced, say in the closing whether the first step is a phone call. 'Start with a conversation' is close, but a parent paying part wants to know she can speak to someone before anything is booked.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent): read top to bottom on iPad, focused on deposits, contracts, who is responsible, after-hours contact and a phone call
No invented brand facts; insolvency cover, after-hours support and first-call format placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored
Deferred business details (fee model, commissions, ranges, real honeymoons, perks) listed as unanswered questions, not penalised or made must-fix

open_questions.question: Does the source pack support any statement on Wedded Wonderland in-trip or after-hours support, insolvency insurance, or the first step being a phone call? If not, the 'questions above already have answers' line should be softened rather than filled.

assumptions: Margaret arrived via a link from her daughter, reading on an iPad, as a parent contributing to the wedding and honeymoon; relevance is 3 because the page is written to the couple, not to her.
Accessibility for elderly relatives is not relevant to a honeymoon for two, so it was not raised.
The 3-minute budget covered the full article read top to bottom, with the FAQ skimmed as it repeats the body.
